principles.name: Every data domain has an owner
principles.statement: Each data domain in DAT-DAC has a single accountable steward responsible for definitions, quality, and lifecycle
principles.rationale: Unowned data drifts in quality and meaning; ownership is the precondition for everything else in data governance
implications: A new data domain cannot be published without a named owner
Disputes over definitions are resolved by the steward, not by committee
Owner accountability is reflected in operational performance reviews

principles.name: Define once, use everywhere
principles.statement: Each concept has a single canonical definition in DAT-DAC; downstream models reference it rather than re-defining
principles.rationale: Parallel definitions create silent divergence and undermine trust in cross-domain analysis
implications: A new concept must be reviewed against existing definitions before introduction
Data products that diverge from the canonical definition must declare it explicitly
Aliases are captured on the canonical concept, not as separate concepts

principles.name: Quality is a producer responsibility
principles.statement: The team producing a data asset is accountable for its quality; consumers should not need to re-cleanse routinely
principles.rationale: Cleansing at point of consumption multiplies effort and produces silent variants
implications: Quality SLAs are part of the data product's contract
Quality issues are routed to the producer team, not absorbed by analytics
Producer instrumentation includes quality metrics, not just volume

principles.name: Privacy by design
principles.statement: Personal data is classified, consent-tracked, and access-controlled from the moment of capture
principles.rationale: Retrofitting privacy onto established data flows is expensive, fragile, and incomplete
implications: Personal-data fields are classified at concept definition, not later
Access rules enforce consent at query time
Anonymisation is a designed transform, not an afterthought

principles.name: Open contracts, open standards
principles.statement: Data products expose stable, versioned, machine-readable contracts; proprietary or undocumented formats are last-resort
principles.rationale: Lock-in to bespoke formats undermines reuse, vendor portability, and ecosystem integration
implications: JSON Schema / Avro / Parquet preferred for serialised data
Vendor data exports must conform to a documented schema

principles.name: Avoid replicating canonical data
principles.statement: Copies of canonical data are minimised; where they exist, they are explicit, expiring, and traceable to source
principles.rationale: Replication multiplies governance surface area and creates undetected divergence
implications: A new copy of canonical data requires justification and an expiry plan
Caches and materialised views are flagged as derivations of a primary source
Sync mechanisms include reconciliation, not just propagation

activity.notes: Reviewed and refined during the 2026-Q1 architecture cycle.
